question: What do we mainly mean by 'sewage' in public health?

options.A: Liquid waste from homes, businesses, and factories
options.B: Treated drinking water stored in community reservoirs
options.C: Industrial runoff containing only chemical fertilizers
options.D: Rainwater collected exclusively from street gutters

explanation: Think of sewage as the used, dirty water flowing away from residential houses, offices, and factories. It carries everyday waste and needs safe management to keep our communities healthy! [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h1)

question: Why is proper sewage disposal so important for community health?

options.A: It completely eliminates all chemical pollutants from manufacturing plants
options.B: It provides essential mineral nutrients for local agricultural soil
options.C: It stops disease-causing germs from reaching drinking water sources
options.D: It lowers the overall temperature of surrounding urban neighborhoods

explanation: When we manage waste safely, we create a barrier that keeps harmful germs away from the water we drink and the places where we live. Great job protecting the public! [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h1)

question: Roughly what percentage of raw sewage is actually water?
explanation: It might surprise you, but raw sewage is almost entirely water—about 99.9%! The solid waste makes up only a tiny fraction of what flows through the pipes. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h2)

question: Where do most harmful germs (pathogens) in domestic sewage come from?

options.B: Atmospheric dust falling into drainage pipes
options.C: Rainwater mixing with soil bacteria outdoors
options.D: Chemical reactions within metal sewer lines

explanation: The disease-causing microorganisms in household sewage mostly come straight from human waste and the gut. That's why keeping waste contained is vital for disease prevention. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h2)

question: Which parasite forms tough outer shells (cysts) that survive normal chlorine treatment in water?
explanation: Giardia is a stubborn protozoan that builds protective cysts. These cysts help it survive tough conditions and shrug off standard amounts of chlorine in water treatment. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h3)

question: A patient comes in with sudden, severe watery diarrhea after drinking untreated water near a broken sewage pipe. Which condition is most likely?
explanation: Cholera is a classic waterborne infection spread by water tainted with human waste. It's famous for causing rapid, severe watery diarrhea that requires quick rehydration. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h3)

question: What is the main job of a septic tank in an individual home's waste system?

options.A: To allow solids to settle and liquids to flow out to a drain field
options.B: To store rainwater for washing clothes and watering gardens
options.C: To incinerate solid waste using high-voltage electric heating
options.D: To pump treated drinking water directly back into household taps

explanation: Think of a septic tank as a settling room: heavy solids sink to the bottom, while the liquid wastewater flows out gently into the underground drain field for natural filtering. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h4)

question: Why is it dangerous to place a septic drain field too close to a shallow drinking water well?

options.A: Roots from nearby trees will block the water pipes completely
options.B: Liquid effluent can seep into the groundwater and spread pathogens
options.C: The weight of the water well can crush the underground septic tank
options.D: The smell of the drain field will ruin the taste of the well water

explanation: If a drain field is too close to a well, untreated wastewater can travel through the soil and contaminate the underground drinking water with dangerous bacteria and viruses. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h4)

question: What big problem can happen with combined city sewer systems during heavy rainstorms?

options.A: Electrical pumps inside homes automatically reverse their flow
options.B: The municipal water pressure drops to zero across the entire city
options.C: Overflows can dump raw, untreated sewage directly into natural water bodies
options.D: Underground pipes freeze solid because of rapid temperature drops

explanation: When storm water and sewage share the same pipes, heavy rains can easily overwhelm the system. When this happens, raw, untreated waste spills straight into local rivers or lakes. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h5)

question: How are separate sanitary sewer networks different from combined systems?

options.A: They carry human wastewater in dedicated pipes separate from storm runoff
options.B: They only operate during daylight hours when industrial plants are open
options.C: They process all solid waste entirely on-site using chemical agents
options.D: They rely exclusively on open drainage ditches running alongside roads

explanation: Separate systems use one set of pipes for sewage and a completely different set for rainwater. This clever design keeps rain floods from overwhelming the treatment plant with raw waste! [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h5)

question: Which stage of wastewater treatment relies mainly on physical screening and letting solids settle?
explanation: Primary treatment is the first physical cleanup step. It uses large screens and settling tanks to catch big debris and let heavy particles drop out of the water. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h6)

question: What is the main goal of secondary wastewater treatment?

options.A: To heat the water until all liquid evaporates into pure water vapor
options.B: To add heavy minerals and nutrients back into agricultural irrigation
options.C: To break down dissolved organic matter using biological microorganisms
options.D: To filter out large plastic bottles and metal cans using iron grates

explanation: In secondary treatment, friendly microorganisms (bacteria) are put to work in large tanks to eat and break down the dissolved organic waste remaining in the water. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h6)

question: What happens to dissolved oxygen in a body of water when raw sewage creates a high biochemical oxygen demand (BOD)?

options.A: Oxygen levels drop significantly, suffocating aquatic life
options.B: Oxygen levels remain completely unchanged year-round
options.C: Oxygen turns directly into toxic chlorine gas bubbles
options.D: Oxygen levels rise rapidly, causing plants to grow too fast

explanation: A high BOD means tiny organisms are gobbling up huge amounts of oxygen to break down the waste. This leaves very little oxygen behind for fish and other aquatic creatures to breathe. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h7)

question: What is a common problem when excess nitrogen and phosphorus from sewage enter water bodies?

options.A: Complete purification of the water within twenty-four hours
options.B: Harmful algal blooms that can release toxins into the water
options.C: An increase in clear visibility and deep-water plant growth
options.D: Immediate freezing of the water surface during warm seasons

explanation: Nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus act like plant fertilizer in water bodies, triggering massive algal overgrowths that block sunlight and can release dangerous toxins. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h7)

question: What is a key role of a public health nurse when it comes to sanitation and disease prevention?

options.A: Educating communities about safe water storage and hand hygiene
options.B: Designing and building municipal underground concrete sewer mains
options.C: Operating heavy excavating machinery to fix broken drain fields
options.D: Manufacturing chemical water purification tablets in a laboratory

explanation: As a nurse, your superpower is education! Teaching families about proper handwashing and safe drinking water habits is one of the best ways to stop infections before they start. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h8)

question: Why must nurses look beyond just treating symptoms when managing a patient with a waterborne illness?

options.A: To test the structural strength of local concrete septic tanks
options.B: To identify and correct the underlying environmental exposure source
options.C: To calculate the financial cost of repairing city water pumps
options.D: To obtain government permits for building new treatment plants

explanation: Treating the illness is only half the battle. If the patient goes back to drinking contaminated water, they will just get sick again. Nurses look at the big picture to fix the root cause! [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h8)
